sources.title: Jason Neelis: Early Buddhist Transmission and Trade Networks, chapter 2 (2011)
sources.note: Indexed original scholarly chapter inspected, especially Table 2.4, printed 156 to 157, and footnote 254 comparing Spink’s short Ajanta chronology with longer alternatives. Direct PDF returns 403. Numerical reigns in the table are scholarly reconstructions, not adopted as exact years here.

sources.title: Hans Bakker: Royal Patronage and Religious Tolerance (2010)
sources.note: Journal of the Royal Asiatic Society 20(4),461 to 475; university repository metadata and indexed original PDF read, especially 469 and 475. Direct PDF 403. Mandhal brick platform and Vaishnava/Shaiva sculptures; differentiated royal, ministerial and subordinate patronage. Same-work DOI 10.1017/S1356186310000301.

sources.title: Dániel Balogh, DHARMA: Pune Charter of Prabhāvatīguptā
sources.note: Direct provisional digital edition. Sanskrit, Southern Brahmi; plates 1v line 1 jitam bhagavatā; lines 7 to 10 family; line 22 regnal year thirteen and engraver. The sample is exact scholarly Roman transliteration, not a claim to reproduce ancient glyph shapes.

sources.title: V. V. Mirashi: Corpus Inscriptionum Indicarum V, Inscriptions of the Vakatakas (1963)
sources.note: Complete ASI volume downloaded. Printed 8/PDF page 113 translation of opening; printed 9/PDF page 115 village exemptions and fiscal rights. Introduction xxix to xxxiii discusses end of branches and Kalachuri succession. Old precise reign dates and literary catastrophe reconstruction not adopted. All passages using this work pooled under this URL.

sources.title: Sontakke and colleagues: Excavation at Nagardhan, Nagpur District, 2015 to 2016
sources.note: Author-uploaded original report, History Today 17, full text directly read. Printed 47 locality 3 Late Satavahana/Vakataka structures; 50 terracottas; 51 to 52 sampled animal remains. These assemblages are not all securely confined to the Vakataka dynasty.

sources.title: Dandekar and colleagues: Second Sealing of the Vakataka Queen Prabhavatigupta from Nagardhan Excavation (2020)
sources.note: Author-uploaded original Bulletin of the Deccan College 80,27 to 30, directly read. Printed 27 to 28 excavation context, conch/name, fingerprints and striations; interpretation as sealing attached to a consignment. DOI 10.2307/48673794 is the same work. No claim that fingerprints belong to the queen.

sources.title: Patel and colleagues: Evaluating the Indian Summer Monsoon intensity using archeological seeds from Vidarbha (2025)
sources.note: Publisher abstract and indexed full author-uploaded original inspected; manuscript 5 to 6, Table 2. Published online 20 November 2025, Holocene 36(1),80 to 94 in 2026. Food list is Early Historic aggregate 300 BCE to 600 CE, not a Vakataka-only diet. Author mirror researchgate.net/publication/397806305 is the same work.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Ajanta Caves
sources.note: Direct official statement: earlier second/first-century BCE caves and later fifth/sixth-century phase under Vakatakas; narrative painting, architecture and sculpture. Runtime Gupta card already attributes a short passage to this URL; cumulative budget checked.

sources.title: Rajesh Singh, IGNCA: Salient Features of Ajanta Caves
sources.note: Direct institutional descriptions of caves 6 Lower,16 and18. Cave 16 sixteen cells and Varahadeva dedication, Cave 18 former drinking-water cistern, Cave 6 sixteen supports for upper storey. Uses broad fifth-century context, not the page’s disputed exact Harishena reign dates.

sources.title: Vaidya and colleagues: Observations on the evidence of horse sacrifice at Nagardhan (2023)
sources.note: Only site chronology in introductory printed 164 is used: occupation from Early Iron Age through medieval phases. Full primary PDF inspected. The horse-sacrifice interpretation and internally conflicting proposed dates are deliberately excluded.
